regime_context: Broad eligibility (14/16 themes) with Base Metals & Copper as the clear leader (score 1.703, breadth 1.0, not crowded). Gold Miners are the challenger with stronger durability (0.79, trend tag) but a 0.42 margin. Rotation is non-directional and no one-narrative dominates; the absolute-trend gate remains the only validated risk-control edge on TSX history.
emerging_watch: Watch for the Gold Miners momentum score (XGD.TO proxy) to exceed Base Metals', which would signal a confirmed leadership handoff and potentially shift the durable-trend narrative toward precious metals. Retire the watch if Base Metals' lead widens beyond 0.8 or if Gold Miners lose trend eligibility.

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals holds the highest momentum score with full breadth, is not crowded, and remains trend-gate eligible. Participation is broad but durability is mixed; trend-following discipline (gate_helps=true) supports risk-controlled exposure while the theme retains leadership. Conviction is low due to small-sample track record and the rank's lack of forward return predictability.
theses.dissent: Mixed durability (0.7) and broad rotation suggest the momentum may be consensus-driven rather than a new structural trend; a copper price rollover could reverse flows abruptly.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO underperforms the S&P/TSX by more than 3% total return over the next 20 trading days

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners rank #2 with the strongest durability (0.79) and a clear trend health tag, are not crowded, and remain eligible. The trend gate's validated drawdown mitigation favours this theme as a complementary overweight if the macro backdrop continues to support precious metals. evidence: Challenger to leader, but margin (0.42) suggests leadership not imminent
